segments.text: Okay, I think everyone is here, so let's get started. Thanks for making time. This is our launch readiness sync for Workflow Automations.
We have about twelve minutes. The plan is to review carryovers, walk through readiness area by area, and leave with clear decisions.
Sounds good. Can we make sure we leave a few minutes at the end for the date conversation? I suspect that's where we'll spend our time.
Yes, that's the last agenda item. Let's start with carryovers from last week. Liam, how did the desktop regression suite go?
That one's done. All four hundred desktop cases are automated and running nightly, and the last three runs were fully green.
Great, I'll mark that complete. Sofia, the empty state designs?
Finished and handed off on Tuesday. Daniel's team already has the final assets, including the dark mode variants.
Hiro, you had the tracking plan draft.
Done as well. The plan covers eighteen events, and I shared it in the launch channel last Thursday for review.
Perfect. Three carryovers closed. Now let's go through readiness. Daniel, engineering first. Where are we?
Core build is feature complete on web. Creating, editing, and scheduling automations all work, and performance is solid.
We load tested with five thousand concurrent automation runs, and the median run time stayed under two seconds.
That's a great number. What about mobile?
Mobile is the soft spot. Viewing automations works well, but editing on mobile is rough, and it's where most of our open bugs are.
Can I jump in on that? Mobile is also my biggest worry from the testing side.
Please, Liam.
Our mobile end to end tests are flaky. About one run in four fails for reasons that aren't real bugs, mostly timing issues with the editor.
So when the suite goes red, I can't tell if we broke something or if it's just noise.
And that's with a team spending half their week on it. I don't want to pretend that's a quick fix.
Is it the drag and drop interaction in the workflow builder? That's a tricky one on touch screens.
Exactly that. The test runner struggles to simulate the drag, so steps fail randomly.
I'll flag that as our first real risk. Flaky mobile tests mean we can't fully trust our signal on that platform.
Agreed, I'll note it as risk number one. Let's park the fix for a second and cover the other areas. Sofia, design status?
Design is complete for launch scope. The only open item is a small polish pass on the schedule picker, which I can finish in two days.
Though, if we cut mobile editing, I'd want to adjust the mobile screens to make view only feel intentional rather than broken.
Good point, hold that thought. Aisha, marketing.
We're in good shape. The launch email is drafted, the landing page is in review, and the demo video is edited and waiting on one last voiceover.
The press embargo lifts the morning of the twelfth, so I need a firm date soon.
Understood. What's missing from your side?
The final changelog copy depends on what actually ships. If features move, I have to rewrite parts of the email, and that takes a couple of days.
That's helpful context for the scope conversation. Marcus, support readiness?
Honestly, this is where I'm nervous. Our help articles are published, but the support macros are not ready.
We need about twelve macros for the most common questions, and so far I've written four.
What's blocking the rest?
Mostly my team's time, plus I need to know the final behavior of the scheduling rules before I can write accurate answers.
The scheduling rules are locked. I can send you the final behavior doc today.
Okay, that's risk number two. Support macros are not ready. Marcus, can you own finishing them?
Yes, I'll take it. Give me until November ninth to have all twelve written, reviewed, and live in the help desk.
Perfect, I'll capture that. Hiro, analytics. How are we looking?
Mixed. Of the eighteen events in the tracking plan, fourteen are instrumented and flowing into the warehouse.
The four missing ones are the important ones for us. Automation created, first run completed, automation paused, and template used.
Is that a launch blocker, or can we backfill later?
We can't backfill events that were never captured, so anything missed at launch is gone for good.
That's our third risk, then. Analytics event gaps. Hiro, what would it take to close them?
About two days of engineering work to add the events, and one day for me to validate them in the warehouse.
I can give him an engineer starting Monday. Let's say the events are in the build by November sixth.
Then I'll validate the same day and confirm in the channel. I'll take the follow up on getting all four events added and verified.
Thank you. Priya, customer success. What are you hearing?
Customers are excited. We have twelve pilot accounts, and nine of them are using automations weekly, which is higher than we expected.
One thing worth sharing is that every single pilot customer asked for approval steps, so a manager can sign off before an automation runs.
Interesting. Is that in scope for this launch?
No, but it came up in ten of the twelve calls. One customer, a large logistics company, said they would roll out to their whole team the day approvals ship.
That's a big signal. I can start exploring the design for approvals while engineering finishes launch work.
I'd rather we not start another feature until launch is stable, but I agree it belongs on the roadmap.
Okay, let's definitely put approvals at the top of the next quarter's discussion. Priya, are the pilot customers ready for launch communication?
Almost. I want to email all twelve personally before the public announcement, since they helped shape this.
That's a great touch. Can you own that?
Yes, I'll send those personal emails by November sixth, so they hear it from us first.
Thank you. Okay, that's the readiness review. Now to the hard conversation: scope and date. Right now we're planning to launch November twelfth.
I'll be direct. With the mobile editor in its current state, I don't think November twelfth is realistic if we ship everything.
I'd rather slip the launch by one week to November nineteenth and ship the full scope properly.
I hear you. My concern is that we've told customers and press November twelfth, and a slip has real cost.
I agree with Maya. The embargo, the webinar invitations, and the partner newsletter are all locked to the twelfth.
If we move, I'm re-coordinating with six different partners, and some won't be able to move.
I understand the cost. But shipping a mobile editor we can't properly test is also a cost.
From a quality view, I can't sign off on mobile editing. With the flaky tests, I can't say it's safe.
Okay, so what if we change the question? What if we keep the date but cut the scope?
Meaning mobile editing becomes view only at launch?
Exactly. Customers can build and edit automations on desktop, and on mobile they can view them, run them, and pause them.
That works for me. It removes most of the risky code and most of the open bugs.
And it shrinks my mobile test surface by about half. I can sign off on that.
Customers mostly build on desktop anyway. In our pilot, ninety percent of edits happened on a laptop.
That matches the data. Mobile edits were under eight percent of all edits during the pilot.
That also cuts the number of support macros I need, because most mobile editing questions go away.
And the changelog barely changes, I just reword the mobile section. That's a few hours, not a few days.
It sounds like we have consensus. Let me state it clearly. We keep the launch date of November twelfth, and we cut mobile editing from launch scope.
Agreed. We'll ship mobile editing as a fast follow once the tests are stable.
Good. That's decision number one. Now, Sofia, you mentioned the mobile screens.
Yes. I'll redesign the mobile automation screen so view only has clear labels and a friendly note that editing is coming soon.
Can you have that to engineering by November fifth?
Thanks. Next, the rollout approach. I'm nervous about turning this on for every customer at once.
Same here. I'd suggest a staged rollout. Twenty percent of customers on launch day, then everyone one week later if the metrics look healthy.
I like that. A twenty percent cohort gives us enough volume to spot problems quickly, and I can set up a dashboard for it.
From a marketing view, I'd still announce on the twelfth. The message becomes rolling out now, available to everyone next week.
Great. So decision number two. We launch to twenty percent of customers on November twelfth, and move to a hundred percent on November nineteenth, assuming the metrics hold.
One question. What counts as healthy metrics? I want us to agree before launch, not after.
I'd propose an error rate under one percent, no increase in support tickets per active account, and automation run success above ninety-eight percent.
Fine from support. Though I'd add that if ticket volume doubles, we pause the rollout.
Good addition. Hiro, can you write those thresholds down in a short rollout criteria doc?
Sure, I'll write that up and share it with everyone by November eighth.
Thank you. Now let's tie the risks together. Marcus, the macros are the one I'm most worried about, since they have a hard dependency on launch.
Right. If the macros aren't live, I can't responsibly support a launch, even at twenty percent.
That sounds like a go or no go condition to me.

I agree. Let's make it formal. We hold a go or no go check on Monday, November tenth, and we only launch if the macros are live, the analytics events are verified, and mobile is stable in view only mode.
I'd add that the desktop regression suite has to be green on the Monday morning run.
Yes, desktop regression green is part of the checklist. That's decision number three.
Liam, since the mobile tests remain flaky, what can we do about them before launch?
With editing cut, I can quarantine the drag and drop tests and keep the rest running. That gives us a reliable signal on view only.
And my team will stabilize the editor tests properly after launch, so mobile editing can come back with confidence.
Then I'll take the cleanup of the mobile suite. I'll quarantine the flaky tests and get three consecutive green runs by November fifth.
Great. Aisha, what do you need from us to finalize the launch materials?
Just the final scope, which we now have. I'll update the changelog and the launch email for view only mobile and send drafts to everyone by November seventh.
Perfect. And I'll handle the roadmap side. I'll update the public roadmap to show mobile editing as coming soon, and approvals as under consideration.
Careful with approvals. I'd say we're exploring it, because customers will hold us to anything we promise.
Fair. Exploring it is. I'll make the roadmap update and send a summary of today's decisions by end of day tomorrow.
Okay, before we wrap, let me recap. Three decisions. Keep November twelfth and cut mobile editing from launch.
Roll out to twenty percent on the twelfth and everyone on the nineteenth. And hold a go or no go check on November tenth.
Three risks. Flaky mobile tests, support macros, and analytics event gaps. Each of them now has an owner and a date.
I'll post it in the launch channel after this call. Anything else before we close?
Just a thank you to everyone. The pilot customers are going to love this.
Thank you all. Great meeting, and let's have a smooth launch.

action_items.task: Finish automating the desktop regression suite and get it running nightly
Hand off final empty state designs including dark mode variants
Draft the analytics tracking plan and share it for review
Quarantine flaky mobile drag and drop tests and get three consecutive green runs
Get all four missing analytics events added and verified in the warehouse
Write, review, and publish all twelve support macros in the help desk
Email all twelve pilot customers personally before the public announcement
Redesign mobile automation screens for a clear view only experience
Update changelog and launch email for view only mobile and send drafts

clips.title: Keeping the launch date by cutting mobile editing
Risk: flaky mobile tests undermine our signal
Every pilot customer is asking for approval steps
